events.name: Group Health Medical Group founded
events.view: He sees the 1947 founders' aim of aligned patient and physician interests as the source of the culture he led.
events.quote: the medical group, uh, came into existence as the Group Health Medical Group back in January, January of 1947.

events.name: Organized medicine's boycott of Group Health physicians
events.view: He describes intense hostility from organized medicine that ended only through a Washington Supreme Court lawsuit.
events.quote: it took a lawsuit that went to the Washington State Supreme Court to, um, to end that discrimination against um Group Health physicians.

prompt.question: can you describe Ruth Health's medical group model and how it shaped your leadership philosophy.

events.name: HIV/AIDS epidemic
events.view: He credits Group Health with early population-based HIV care in primary care clinics, which drew many HIV patients.
events.quote: we created some of the very earliest population-based approaches to HIV disease.

retellable.title: Three Swedish medical students
retellable.summary: Planning a career in law or journalism, he spent a year in Sweden living with three medical students. Going on rounds and home visits with them convinced him medicine could best serve social justice.
retellable.quote: I started going on rounds with them and especially making home visits. And, uh, I came to believe that, uh, my interest in social justice and in making the world a better place, could better be served by medicine
retellable.why: Shows a chance encounter shaping a mission-driven physician career.

retellable.title: "Do something about it": the white paper
retellable.summary: Overworked family doctors were covering clinic, hospital rounds and urgent care. When his wife told him to stop complaining and act, he wrote a white paper proposing an urgent care department.
retellable.quote: my wife said to me, well, do something about it if you feel so strongly. So I wrote a white paper, I called it a white paper, about changing and changes in medicine,
retellable.why: A plain lesson in turning frustration into leadership.

retellable.title: Worth half the deal: the "naked doctors"
retellable.summary: During the Group Health sale, the medical group had its own investment banker ask United what its offer would be worth without the physicians. The answer was half, proving the group's value.
retellable.quote: Our instructor asked our investment banker to explore with United what would the deal be worth without us? And it was literally 50% less.
retellable.why: Demonstrates the power of an independent medical group in negotiations.
